texts: good. the redistributing, the Council as agent, the mire-essence reserves as what is redistributed and the once-per-full-moon recurrence are all carried; the lunar cycle sits in a period slot meant for time units, but everything the parse asserts about it is true.
good. "each lantern-station" becomes a rule that can fire, giving every station its own reporting event, with that station's monthly production as what is reported and the Council as recipient.

mixed: the parse itself is usable and faithful — a warden linked to Cauldron Hall, reporting the essence reserve to the Council. The risk is the capitalized "Warden": the translator has to guess between treating it as an ordinary noun attached to the named hall (what it did here) and treating "Cauldron Hall Warden" as a single proper name, and the two guesses produce different symbols, so this warden may not line up with mentions in your other sentences. Rewrite as "The warden of Cauldron Hall reports the essence reserve to the Council." — a lowercase head noun settles the choice without changing the meaning.

bad: "for the coming month" is read as when the allocating happens, so the parse claims the Council does the allocating during the coming month rather than that the allocation covers that month — a different statement, and the coverage period is lost. Rewrite as "The Council allocates mire-essence to the stations to cover the coming month." which states the period the essence is meant to last without asserting when the handover itself takes place.
